name: Judith Dai
life: “I still remember showing a public planner the last empty bus.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Judith knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I work in traffic planning. I brought the ride log to the meeting that was going to cut another late bus.
appearance: Judith has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Look for a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. In conversation Judith turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Judith loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To restore a late service using actual shift journeys.
family: Rae Villa is Judith’s younger cousin. Judith brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Rae checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The trust with a typo*, Rae says, “I threw out the letter as a joke. The post carrier came back after work to tell me it counted.”
connections: Ariel Crawford. A lift promised through eye treatment becomes actual evidence for a late-bus case. Also in the story is Patricia Ramos (commuter).

reactions.situation: A shift worker is late to the meeting point
reactions.response: Judith checks whether waiting will make the whole shift late and tells the rider the decision.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Judith gets the people at the next doorway away from the smoke and asks a bystander to make the call.

reactions.response: Judith offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
